meta.title: Collatz max-odd sieve -- visualisation data
meta.map: S_q(n) = (3n+q)/2^b, b = v2(3n+q), n odd, q odd, 3 nmid q

notation.L: number of odd elements of a cycle
notation.M: largest odd element of a cycle
notation.y_k: k-th odd predecessor going backward from M (y_0 = M)
notation.b_k: halvings on the k-th backward hop: 3 y_k + q = 2^{b_k} y_{k-1}
notation.a_j: forward halvings: x_j = (3 x_{j-1} + q)/2^{a_j}, x_0 = M.  b_j = a_{L+1-j}

meta.novelty_note: Nothing in T0-T8 is new.  T0/T1/T6/T7 are published (some 45+ years ago); T2 is the literature's standard local-maximum analysis; T3/T4/T5/T8 are one-line corollaries of folklore that were not found written verbatim -- the weakest possible form of novelty, and not to be presented as a result.  The floor (backward) / ceiling (forward) parity-vector machinery is the standard Eliahou / Simons-de Weger apparatus.  Cautionary precedent: Kaneda's own acknowledgements (Fib. Quart. 53(2), p.174) record that Lagarias and a referee told him his Section 2 results were not new, only the proofs.

verification_limit.source: D. Barina, J. Supercomputing 81, 810 (2025); project page pcbarina.fit.vutbr.cz, retrieved 2026-08-26
verification_limit.meaning: all n < 2075*2^60 verified to reach 1; hence any nontrivial q=1 cycle has minimum element > this

min_odd_elements.source: Hercher, J. Integer Seq. 26 (2023), Art. 23.3.5, Corollary 29 (hypothesis X0 >= 1536*2^60, met by Barina 2025)
min_odd_elements.caveat: the combination Barina-2025 + Hercher-Cor.29 was inferred, not found stated in print

min_m_cycles.source: Hercher 2023: no nontrivial Collatz m-cycle with m <= 91

theorems.short: 3 | n  =>  n has no odd predecessor
theorems.statement: q odd, 3 nmid q.  If p is odd and 3|p then p has no odd S_q-predecessor, hence lies on no S_q-cycle.  Every element of every S_q-cycle is coprime to 3.
theorems.hypotheses: q odd, 3 nmid q.  Nothing else.
theorems.proof: 3y+q = 2^b p; mod 3 the LHS is q and the RHS is 0, so 3|q -- contradiction.
theorems.prior_art: textbook folklore.  Kaneda, Fib. Quart. 53(2) (2015) p.169; Brox, Acta Arith. 92 (2000); Tao, Forum of Math Pi 10 (2022) e12.  DO NOT CLAIM.

theorems.statement: M the max of an S_q-cycle => v2(3M+q) >= 2, i.e. 4 | 3M+q, i.e. M = q (mod 4).  q=1: M = 1 (mod 4).
theorems.hypotheses: NONE beyond q>0 odd, 3 nmid q, M the cycle max.  GROUND_TRUTH's 'M > q' is superfluous.
theorems.proof: S_q(M) <= M gives 2^b >= 3 + q/M > 3, so b >= 2.  Refinements: M < q forces b >= 3; M = q forces b = 2 exactly.
theorems.prior_art: Brox 2000 calls such an odd number 'descending' in his opening definitions; the local-max decomposition of Simons-de Weger (Acta Arith. 117 (2005)) builds it in.  DO NOT CLAIM.
theorems.corrects_ground_truth: GROUND_TRUTH says M>q is required for T1 and lists (q=17,{1,5}) and (q=23,{7,11}) as counterexamples.  Both satisfy T1 (v2(32)=5, v2(56)=3).  They are counterexamples to T2 only.

theorems.statement: M the max of an S_q-cycle with M >= q => b_1 = 1: the unique in-cycle odd predecessor of M is y_1 = (2M-q)/3.  Forces 3 | 2M-q, i.e. M = 2q (mod 3); q=1: M = 2 (mod 3).
theorems.hypotheses: M >= q suffices.  'L >= 2' is redundant: M > q already forces L >= 2 (see FP).
theorems.proof: y_b = (2^b M - q)/3 < M <=> M(2^b - 3) < q; for b >= 2 that needs M < q.
theorems.tightness: TIGHT: q=17 cycle {5,1} has M=5<q and b_1=2; q=23 cycle {11,7} has M=11<q and b_1=2.  CONVERSE FALSE: b_1=1 does not imply M>q (e.g. q=11 cycle {7,1}).
theorems.prior_art: the standard local-maximum analysis; Brox's 'descendent', Kaneda 2015 Thm 2.1.  DO NOT CLAIM.

theorems.short: at most one odd predecessor below p
theorems.statement: q odd, 3 nmid q, p odd > 0 with 3 nmid p.  Odd predecessors of p are exactly y_b=(2^b p - q)/3 for b >= 1 in one fixed parity class (parity forced by p mod 3), 2^b p > q; y_b is automatically odd and strictly increasing in b.  Hence p has AT MOST ONE odd predecessor strictly below itself, for every q.
theorems.hypotheses: none beyond the above; in particular no relation between p and q.
theorems.proof: y_b < p <=> q/p < 2^b < 3 + q/p, a window of additive length 3; 2^{b+2}-2^b = 3*2^b >= 6 > 3.
theorems.prior_art: elementary/folklore (backward Collatz tree).  DO NOT CLAIM.

theorems.proof: CRT on T1 (M = q mod 4) and T2 (M = 2q mod 3).
theorems.prior_art: not found verbatim in the literature, but it is CRT on two folklore facts.  Describe as 'a folklore corollary', never as a result.

theorems.statement: M > q => M != 5q (mod 9).  With T3: M = 17q or 29q (mod 36).  q=1: M = 17 or 29 (mod 36).
theorems.hypotheses: M > q (needed: the proof uses b_1 = 1).
theorems.proof: y_1=(2M-q)/3 is on the cycle so 3 nmid y_1; 3|y_1 <=> 9|2M-q <=> M = 5q (mod 9).
theorems.tightness: TIGHT: cycles with M = 5q (mod 9) exist and all have M < q or L = 1 -- e.g. q=119 M=19, q=355 M=47, q=503 M=67, q=833 M=133.
theorems.prior_art: the 3-adic predecessor-set pruning is standard; Wirsching, Springer LNM 1681 (1998) is the book-length treatment.  Not found verbatim.
theorems.corrects_ground_truth: GROUND_TRUTH's 'recurses to higher powers of 3' is misleading.  T0 ALONE saturates at M = 2,8 (mod 9): the surviving set mod 3^{k+1} stays exactly 2*3^{k-1} classes (density 2/9) at every depth.  Every further 3-adic gain comes from the SIZE condition T6, not from T0.

theorems.statement: CORRECTED: M the max of an S_q-cycle with M > 11q/7 => b_2 <= 2.  (GROUND_TRUTH's q=1, M>=2 version is true; its 'L >= 3' hypothesis is wrong.)
theorems.corrects_ground_truth: GROUND_TRUTH says T5 needs L >= 3 'else y_2 = M wraps'.  FALSE: q=37, cycle 53 -> 49 -> 23 -> 53 has L=3, M=53>q=37, y_2=49<M (no wrap) and b_2=3.  And the q=7,M=11 example is not a wrap artifact: there the exact inequality holds with EQUALITY (77 <= 77) because 7M = 11q.
theorems.prior_art: the local-max neighbourhood arithmetic of Steiner (1977) / Simons (Math. Comp. 74 (2005)).  Not found verbatim; a trivial sharpening.

theorems.statement: Exact.  For M above a (small!) threshold this is equivalent to B_k <= floor(k log2 3).
theorems.hypotheses: the floor form needs M > max_{j<=k} g(j); see sieve_layers.floor_rule_thresholds.
theorems.corrects_ground_truth: GROUND_TRUTH's 'M >= 2^68' is wildly over-conservative: for all k <= 20 the floor rule is equivalent to the exact test as soon as M > 17344, and g(2) = 1 reproduces T5's 'M >= 2'.
theorems.prior_art: standard.  Kaneda 2015 Thm 2.1 inequality (2.3) is the mirror image (from the minimum); same device in Eliahou (Discrete Math. 118 (1993)), Halbeisen-Hungerbuehler (Acta Arith. 78 (1997)), Simons-de Weger (2005).  DO NOT CLAIM.

theorems.statement: The cycle equation; forces 2^B > 3^L and B/L > log2 3, and closing a cycle needs 2^B/3^L within ~1/M of 1.
theorems.prior_art: Boehm & Sontacchi, Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei 64 (1978) 260-264 (already Lean-formalised at ccchallenge.org); the Diophantine consequence is Crandall, Math. Comp. 32 (1978) 1281-1292, via Baker 1968 / Rhin 1987.  ABSOLUTELY NOT NEW.

theorems.statement: q=1: the max odd of a cycle satisfies M != 9 (mod 16).  With T3: M = 5, 17 or 29 (mod 48).
theorems.proof: M=16s+9 => 3M+1 = 4(12s+7), v2 = 2 exactly, x_1 = 12s+7; 3x_1+1 = 2(18s+11), v2 = 1 exactly, x_2 = 18s+11 > 16s+9 = M for every s >= 0, contradicting maximality.
theorems.prior_art: elementary; almost certainly folklore.  This is the j=2 case of the standard forward coefficient-stopping-time sieve (Terras, Acta Arith. 30 (1976)).

theorems.statement: Every S_q fixed point satisfies n(2^b - 3) = q with b >= 2, hence n <= q.  So the 'L >= 2' hypothesis in T2/T3/T4 is redundant given M > q.
FALSE.  c_k grows like 2^{B_k}, not O(1).  Real counterexample: q=5, cycle 49 -> 19 -> 31 -> 49 has M=49 and B_3 = 5 > 4 = floor(3 log2 3).

theorems.short: the T4 recursion is a forced chain at every depth
theorems.statement: FALSE from depth 4 on.  The prefix (b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4) = (1,1,1,3) has B_4 = 6 and 2^6 = 64 < 81 = 3^4, so the size test y_4 <= M is vacuous there and b_4 is not determined.  The recursion is a BRANCHING sieve, not a forced chain.

wheel.description: Classification of odd n = 1,3,5,... as candidates for being the largest odd element M of a q=1 cycle.  One character per odd number, index i <-> n = 2i+1.

a.why: 3n+1 = 2 (mod 4), so v2 = 1 and S(n) = (3n+1)/2 > n: n ascends, cannot be the max

b.why: 3y+1 is never divisible by 3, so n has no odd predecessor at all

c.why: then (2n-1)/3 is not an integer; the parity of b is forced even, and every odd predecessor (4n-1)/3, (16n-1)/3, ... exceeds n

legend.digit: survives the mod-12 wheel (n = 5 mod 12); the digit is the deepest 3-adic sieve level k it also survives (see sieve_layers.mod3)

wheel.caveat: Rules a/b/c are exclusions for the maximum of a q=1 cycle with M > q = 1, i.e. for n >= 3.  n = 1 IS the maximum of the trivial cycle {1} and is nevertheless labelled 'c' -- that single index is the one place the wheel over-claims, because T2 needs M > q strictly (at M = q the 'predecessor' of M is M itself).  The DIGIT (deep level) is only a valid exclusion for M above the corresponding threshold in sieve_layers.floor_rule_thresholds -- do not colour a small n 'excluded at level 6' without saying so.

backward_tree.description: Surviving backward halving-vectors (b_1..b_k) from M, for q=1 and M large enough that T6's exact test is the floor rule.  b_1 = 1 is forced (that is T2).
backward_tree.rule: b_j >= 1 and B_j <= floor(j*log2 3) for every j <= k
backward_tree.encoding: child_counts[k-1] is a digit string, one digit per node at depth k-1 (in canonical order), giving how many children it has.  A node at depth k-1 with prefix sum B has exactly children b = 1..(floor(k*log2 3) - B), in that order.  Root = depth 0, B_0 = 0. Reconstruct: B_k = B_{k-1} + b.  drift_k = B_k - k*log2(3) (always <= 0); ratio 2^{B_k}/3^k = 2^{drift_k}.
backward_tree.N_k_note: N(k) for k = 1..40, by DP over prefix sums; matches the explicit tree for k <= max_depth.  Unconstrained would be 8^k-ish.

growth.fit: N(k) ~ 1.235 * lambda^k * k^(-1.51) empirically over k = 100..300 (the k^(-3/2) is the standard ballot/first-passage correction)

sturmian.note: the step word w_k = floor(k lg3) - floor((k-1) lg3) in {1,2} is Sturmian with slope lg3 - 1

sieve_layers.description: Two independent sieves on the residue of M, plus their CRT product.

mod3.what: 3-adic: for each floor-admissible backward vector at depth k, M mod 3^k is pinned and T0 (3 nmid y_k) kills one of the three lifts to mod 3^{k+1}.  Survivors = union.
mod3.requires: M > max_{j<=k} floor_rule_thresholds[j] (else use T6's exact test)

t0_only_saturates.note: WITHOUT the size condition, T0 alone gives nothing past mod 9: the survivor set is always exactly M = 2, 8 (mod 9) lifted, i.e. 2*3^{k-1} of 3^{k+1} classes, density 2/9 at every depth.  Reason: 2 has order 6 mod 9, so both parities of b_{j+1} still realise all three residues of y_{j+1} mod 3, and a legal b_{j+1} always exists.  GROUND_TRUTH's 'T4 recurses to higher powers of 3' is misleading.

mod2.what: 2-adic: the forward mirror.  x_j = (3 x_{j-1}+1)/2^{a_j} <= M for all j <=> A_j >= ceil(j log2 3); a_j depends only on low bits of M, so this is a mod-2^a condition.  a=2 is T1; the first genuine refinement is at a=4 (T8: M != 9 mod 16).
mod2.limit_note: SATURATES.  The whole forward 2-adic sieve is worth about 1.8043 bits, forever; extra depth buys nothing.  This is the negative-drift random-walk survival probability (Terras coefficient-stopping-time framework).

hard_classes.note: mod48 = mod16 refinement intersected with T3 (M = 5 mod 12)

combined_crt.note: The moduli 2^a and 3^{k+1} are coprime so the densities multiply.  CAVEAT: this is exact as a statement about residue classes surviving two independently defined sieves; it is a joint statement about an actual cycle only when L >= k + j + 1, so that the k backward and j forward elements from M are distinct.
combined_crt.verdict: The sieve cannot close the problem: the 2-adic half caps at 1.80 bits and the 3-adic half decays at best geometrically in k while the modulus grows 1.585 bits per k.  The surviving-class COUNT grows.

floor_rule_thresholds.note: g(k) = the largest M for which T6's exact test M(2^{B_k}-3^k) <= c_k still admits a vector that the floor rule B_k <= floor(k lg3) rejects.  So the floor rule is equivalent to T6 for all depths <= k as soon as M > max_{j<=k} g(j).  g(2) = 1 reproduces T5's 'M >= 2' (sharp ratio 11q/7); GROUND_TRUTH's 2^68 is wildly over-conservative.

forward_2adic.method: For 120000 real odd M starting at 2^24+1, run the full forward Syracuse orbit to 1 and keep M iff no x_j exceeds M.  Compare the observed residues mod 2^a against the predicted survivor sets, and the observed density against the DP limit.

backward_3adic.method: Honest backward DFS on REAL integers M in [1000001, 1000001+2*60000), q=1, using only the exact tests y_j <= M, 3 nmid y_j and integrality.  No residue arithmetic, no floor rule, and b_1 = 1 is NOT assumed (it comes out as an output).  Compared against the residue-derived mod-3^{k+1} survivor sets.

cycles.description: All S_q cycles found by exhaustive forward search from every odd start <= max(400, 30q), value cap 5e6, step cap 4000, for the listed q.  This finds every cycle having an element in that range; it is NOT a proof that no other cycle exists for these q.

fields.odds: the cycle's odd elements in FORWARD order starting at M
fields.a: forward halvings, a_j = v2(3*odds[j-1]+q); sum = B
fields.b: backward halvings = reverse(a); b_1 = a[L-1] is the hop into M
fields.chk: per-cycle theorem verdicts, null = not applicable (L = 1).  cmp = sign of M-q; r = M/q; b1,b2 = first two BACKWARD halvings; T0: every element coprime to 3.  T1: (M-q)%4 == 0.  T2: b1 == 1 (claimed only when M > q).  T3: (M-5q)%12 == 0 (only when M > q).  T4: (M-5q)%9 != 0 (only when M > q).  T5: b2 <= 2 (only when 7M > 11q).

size_refinements.note: T1's refinements by the sign of M - q.  The hypothesis M > q works the OPPOSITE way from what GROUND_TRUTH suggests: M < q gives a STRICTLY STRONGER conclusion.

M_eq_q.claim: M = q => M is a fixed point (L = 1) and v2(3M+q) = 2 exactly

fixed_points.claim: FP: n(2^b - 3) = q with b >= 2, so every fixed point has M <= q; hence M > q => L >= 2

sharp_T5_threshold.note: cycles with 7M = 11q exactly -- the sharp T5 threshold; all have b_2 = 3

cycles.summary_note: T2_given_M_ge_q_INCLUDING_FIXED_POINTS fails exactly on the M = q fixed points (L = 1, b = 2), where the 'predecessor' of M is M itself -- so the honest hypothesis for T2 is M > q (equivalently M >= q AND L >= 2).  T5_bad_hypothesis_L_ge_3 is the row that REFUTES GROUND_TRUTH's 'T5 needs L >= 3': there are cycles with L >= 3, M > q and b_2 = 3.  The size hypothesis M > 11q/7 has no failures.

highlights.q7_5_11: M = 11 > q = 7 but 7M = 11q exactly, the SHARP T5 threshold: b_2 = 3
highlights.q37_23_49_53: L = 3, M = 53 > q = 37, y_2 = 49 < M (no wrap), b_2 = 3 -- kills the 'L >= 3' hypothesis
highlights.q5_49_19_31: M = 49, B_3 = 5 > 4 = floor(3 lg3) -- the FALSE-1 counterexample

diophantine.description: T7 forces 2^B > 3^L, so B = floor(L log2 3) + 1 at best.  Writing 2^B = prod over the cycle of (3 + q/n_i) and using min <= n_i <= M gives 1/excess >= min  and  M >= 1/excess, with excess = 2^{B/L} - 3.  So a cycle of length L is possible only if its minimum element is at most 1/excess(L).
diophantine.records_note: Every L <= 20000 at which min_bound sets a new record.  The best of them, L = 15601, still only permits a cycle minimum of 2.86e+08 -- about 1e13 times below the verified bound.  Note L = 1 gives min_bound = 1: the only q=1 fixed point is 1 itself (the L=1 case of Steiner's no-nontrivial-circuit theorem).
diophantine.verdict: For every L <= 200 the bound on the cycle minimum is at most 12824 (at L = 200), which is ~1e17 times below Barina's verified bound of 2075*2^60.  So no q=1 cycle of any of these lengths exists -- the approximation B/L to log2 3 has to be astronomically good.

trajectories.description: Odd-step (Syracuse) trajectories.  n[i] are the odd values, b[i] = v2(3*n[i]+q) the halvings, n[i+1] = (3*n[i]+q)>>b[i].  Step i ASCENDS iff n[i+1] > n[i] iff 2^{b[i]} < 3 + q/n[i] (for q=1 and n>1 that is exactly b[i] == 1).

list.note: the only known q=1 cycle: fixed point 1 -> 1
the user's seed: 3*7+1 = 22, next odd is 11 > 7, so 7 ascends.  7 = 3 (mod 4) = T1
T8 in action: 9 = 9 (mod 16), and 9 -> 7 -> 11 with 11 > 9, so 9 cannot be a maximum.  Generally M=16s+9 gives x_1 = 12s+7 then x_2 = 18s+11 > M
11 = 3 (mod 4) so T1 excludes it -- NOT because 'you need a bigger odd to reach 11' (7 -> 11 with 7 < 11)
the classic: 41 odd steps, peaks at 3077
q=7 cycle 5 -> 11 -> 5; 7M = 11q exactly, the sharp T5 threshold
q=17 cycle 1 -> 5 -> 1; M = 5 < q so T2 fails, b_1 = 2
q=37 cycle 53 -> 49 -> 23 -> 53: L=3, M=53>q=37, y_2=49<M (no wrap), b_2=3 -- refutes the 'L>=3' hypothesis for T5
